blocks.text: The greenhouse effect is the natural process in which gases in the Earth's atmosphere, greenhouse gases (GHGs), trap the heat radiated from the Earth's surface: they let sunlight pass but stop heat escaping directly into space, keeping the Earth warm enough for life.

The concentrations of these gases, especially CO2, have risen markedly, mainly through the use of fossil fuels to run machines, drive vehicles, heat homes and generate electricity. The resulting enhanced, unnatural warming of the atmosphere is the major negative impact of human activities on the environment.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: According to the World Meteorological Organization, CO2 was about 280 parts per million before industrialisation and reached 428 ppm in 2026, still rising; the mean global temperature has risen about 1 C since 1900. Pakistan contributes less than 1% of global greenhouse emissions but is ranked among the ten countries most vulnerable to climate change.
